name: Alex's Reader
subtitle: One app, kept fresh.
description: The private build of Reader, published for the people it was made for.

apps.name: Reader
apps.subtitle: Books, catalogs, and volume-key page turns.
apps.localizedDescription: A personal e-book reader. Reads EPUB, FB2, MOBI, AZW3 and CBZ, pulls books from any OPDS catalog, and turns pages with a swipe, a tap or the hardware volume keys. The page is set like a printed one: a running head, a text block and a folio, in six themes.

privacy.NSCameraUsageDescription: Reader watches the front camera for a held blink and turns the page. It runs only while a book is open, nothing is recorded, and nothing leaves this phone.

versions.localizedDescription:
New at the bottom of Statistics: Ask ChatGPT. Preview and copy or share a request based on your reading history to discover books outside your library. Nothing is sent until you choose to share.
Rate books from one to five stars when marking them read, or change the rating later in reading history. Your ratings are saved in backups and included in ChatGPT requests.
All finished and unstarted books are selected by default, including books you marked read manually. You can leave out any books before sharing; book files, notes and bookmarks stay out of the request.

Fixed blinks and tongue gestures being refused when the camera reads your face unsteadily — lying down, or in a dim room.
Head turns are no longer paused by simply holding the phone. Only real movement pauses them now, and a knock costs a third of a second rather than the second and a bit it used to.
New under Settings → Camera: Show what the camera sees. A small readout over the page saying whether the camera can see your face and how close a gesture came — for when one does nothing and you cannot tell why.

Walking with a book open no longer turns pages by itself. Head turns now wait until the phone is holding still, and start working again a moment after you stop.
The dot at the top of the page goes hollow while they are waiting, so you can tell. Blinks and the tongue are unaffected — they work on the move as they always did.

Turn pages without touching the phone: hold a blink, turn your head, or put your tongue out. Every gesture is off until you switch it on, in Settings under Camera, and you choose what each one does.
The phone taps you when a page has turned, so you know it worked without opening your eyes.
Before you switch any of it on: the front camera runs the whole time a book is open, which costs battery. Nothing is recorded and nothing leaves the phone.

A book you have been sent goes straight onto your shelf now: tap Share wherever it arrived — Telegram, Mail, Files, a browser — and pick Reader. If it is a book you already have, it asks whether to replace your copy, keep both, or leave it alone.
Tapping a footnote no longer finishes the book. Following one to the notes at the back and coming straight back used to mark it read, date it today and file it away with the books you have finished.
An evening of reading counts as one sitting again rather than several, and what a sitting was worth is the reading you did in it instead of every jump. Sittings were too many and too short, and the hour-in-one-sitting badge now unlocks when you have earned it.
Switches, and the tick on a badge you have earned, take their colour from the page you read on instead of coming out hard black in the warmer themes.

Libraries that ask you to sign in now work: the password is asked for in the app and remembered, and it holds for the searches, covers and books behind it. Standard Ebooks is one of them.
Marking a book read no longer takes the year as your whole answer and shuts the calendar. Pick the date, then tap to use it — and the months are in your language, with weeks starting on Monday.
Books you have finished are their own group at the foot of your shelf now, most recently finished first, so a library marked read in one afternoon is in the order you actually finished things.
Pictures in a library you browse no longer come out stretched, and one that never arrives leaves no broken icon behind.

Your reading now sits on the Home Screen. Add the Reader widget and your run of days, today's reading and how much of your daily goal is behind you are there without opening anything.
Three sizes: the smallest holds the streak and today, the largest adds this week and the book you are part-way through — tap that one to carry straight on reading.
The widget takes whichever reading theme you use, and is written in your own language.

Arrange your books onto shelves you name yourself — hold a book to lift it and drag it onto one, and a book can sit on as many shelves as you like.
Send a book to somebody, or save it into Files and so to iCloud Drive, from the book's own menu.
Marking a book read now asks when you finished it, so the ones you read years ago land on the right day rather than today. You can change the date later from the book's page.
A book's reading figures are one tap from the shelf, the type settings can be put back the way they came, and today's total fits inside the goal circle again in Ukrainian and Russian.

A new Stats tab counts your reading: how long, on which days, how fast, and how many days in a row you have kept it up.
Every book gets a page of that too, down to how much longer it will take at the pace you actually read.
Save your whole library — books, bookmarks and where you are in each one — into a single file you can keep in iCloud Drive, then put it back on any phone.
The app now speaks Ukrainian and Russian as well as English, following your phone unless you choose for yourself in Settings.

Bookmark the page you are on with the ribbon at the top, and get back to it from the contents.
Choose how a page turns — it can slide, lift off the top, or lay the next page over it.
Scrolling instead of pages now really scrolls: drag the text with your finger and it carries on when you let go.
Fixed a theme change leaving the old colour around the edges of the page, and a picker that offered nothing but ZIP files.

Tap a picture in a book to open it full screen — pinch or double-tap for a closer look.
Tap the small number beside a word to read its note, and the button in the corner brings you back to the page you were on.

A proper app icon — a walnut page, instead of the blue placeholder.
Nothing else in the app has changed.

The first build: your own shelf, the catalogs you pull books from, and a page set like a printed one — running head, text block, page number.
Page numbers stopped drifting when you crossed into a new chapter, the controls no longer swallow a page turn, and the shelf finds Cyrillic titles.
